Green: local read-after-write/restart, complete entity/writer classification, no branch/project leakage, safe expired-lease recovery and stable replicated IDs. Provider schema changes introduced here require migrations for each affected supported provider, not Dolt alone.

LeaseLostDuringWriteRejected means admission after expiry/fence change is rejected and takeover waits for an already-admitted transaction; it does not demand aborting a transaction legitimately holding the gate through completion.

## 8. Ph3: seed migration and project recovery export

Requirements: FR-MCP-187, FR-MCP-182/184, FR-MCP-AUDIT-001 and the reconciled backfill contracts. A missing domain or branch blocks routing changes. Same-work/different-ID candidates require review; never rewrite historical text references.

Migration acceptance also covers multi-project separation, soft-deleted rows, decimal/UTC/binary/Unicode edge cases, complete promoted session graphs, hub-bound audit, derived-index rebuild and inert imported operational records. Inject death after target batch commit before acknowledgement, before provider switch and after switch before reopening. Dry-run and failed verification must preserve source bytes and active routing. ===== EF provider policy sites (prerelease / maintained / bespoke / GA) ===== docs/plans/2026-11-10-federation-library-options.md:53:Key fit questions: can server-enforced workspace filters prevent foreign-workspace data access; can hub-owned fields remain authoritative; do mixed-provider schemas, FK graphs, tombstones and canonical identifiers match the approved data model; does direct table synchronization preserve required domain validation and audit behavior; can existing data be provisioned without destructive schema work? A need for broad bespoke providers or engine modifications would undermine the speed benefit. docs/plans/2026-11-10-federation-library-options.md:82:The operator identified Git's distributed model as the intended federation model and approved branches for this release. Evaluate native Git or a maintained binding for actual history/branch/merge operations. Git's three-way content merging is available through [git merge-file](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-merge-file); ancestry selection is a separate responsibility described by [git merge-base](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-merge-base). Reuse these facilities instead of implementing a bespoke merge algorithm. docs/plans/2026-11-10-federation-dolt-bdpv4.md:72:Per the operator decision of 2026-11-11 (MEMORY-PREFERENCE-002; architecture section 8), a prerelease or community-fork EF10 provider, patched by this project and contributed upstream as needed, is an accepted dependency for the Dolt project context, so the absence of a GA-maintained provider does not block B1. If no EF10 provider can be made to drive Dolt's required semantics even with reasonable patching, report concrete options for approval; do not downgrade the repository silently or ship a bespoke from-scratch provider without the operator's agreement. This plan is executable through Ph0 but is not implementation-ready for later slices until these evidence-dependent choices are locked. docs/plans/exports/Federation-2026-11-10-R2.html:8:

The operator additionally requires Dolt as the fourth supported database, retaining SQLite, PostgreSQL and SQL Server, with appropriate schema migrations and a separate data migration tool from all three original providers. This document adopts that planning direction. The exact maintained EF Core provider/package version and pinned Dolt image must pass the compatibility gate before implementation dependencies are installed. Dolt's relational cell/schema merge is the proposed interpretation of Git-style merging; literal line-level text merging is not claimed.

docs/plans/exports/Federation-2026-11-10-R2.html:697:

Ph0 selects a maintained EF10-compatible MySQL provider after executing real schema/query/transaction tests against a pinned Dolt image. Do not silently downgrade EF, install a prerelease provider, or write a bespoke EF provider if compatibility fails; report concrete alternatives for the operator. Test collations/case sensitivity, maximum index/key lengths, decimal precision, UTC timestamps, GUID/binary/text/JSON mappings, identity generation, optimistic concurrency, FK/delete semantics, raw SQL, query translation, migrations and parameterization. SQLite-specific search SQL must use a provider-compatible derived-index path rather than fail on Dolt.

docs/plans/exports/Federation-2026-11-10-R2.html:795:

If a maintained EF10-compatible provider is unavailable, report concrete options for approval; do not downgrade the repository silently. This plan is executable through Ph0 but is not implementation-ready for later slices until these evidence-dependent choices are locked.

Critical-dependency feasibility: can the single load-bearing dependency (a maintained EF Core 10 provider driving Dolt over the MySQL wire on net10.0) be satisfied without violating the operator's dependency rules? docs/plans/2026-11-11-federation-correctness-evaluation.md:25:- 3.2 The plan is structured to answer "correct" before committing (observation). Ph0 is a disposable feasibility harness with twelve blocking outputs (B1-B12), all initial status "unproven," and it explicitly forbids silent EF downgrade, a prerelease provider, or a bespoke provider; it requires reporting concrete alternatives if compatibility fails. Nothing in Ph1-Ph8 is authorized until Ph0 is accepted. So the plan already treats the engine/provider bet as a gated spike, not an assumption. (Receipt: 2026-11-10-federation-dolt-bdpv4.md section 5; architecture.md section 8.) docs/plans/2026-11-11-federation-correctness-evaluation.md:32: - Pomelo.EntityFrameworkCore.MySql, the provider DoltHub itself uses, has NO GA EF Core 10 release. Its latest 9.0.0 constrains EF Core to the 9.0.x range; mixing any EF Core 10 package yields NU1107/NU1608. The EF10 port (PR 2031) is open and unmerged; the tracking issue has been open with a "soon" since Oct 2025. 1	# Federation correctness evaluation: is Dolt-versioned federation the CORRECT way to proceed?
2	
3	Author: ClaudeCode. Date: 2026-11-11. Status: DRAFT decision-support (built while the plan-readiness HV iterated toward AGREE). This is not a requirement, not a plan, and not an approval. It is the case the operator asked for: after HV establishes a VALID way to proceed, decide whether it is the CORRECT way. The architecture decision is the operator's; this document builds the evidence, criteria, risks and a labeled recommendation so he can make it.
4	
5	Observation vs inference is marked throughout. Receipts (web sources) are listed at the end.
6	
7	## 1. The two different questions
8	
9	- VALID (what HV answers): is the plan internally consistent, decision-complete, and free of rule violations, so a less-capable implementer could execute it without inventing unstated decisions? The R2->R4 HV loop answers this for the packet.
10	- CORRECT (this document): is Dolt-versioned-relational federation, with the independent-node + hub + guarded-publication architecture, the right thing to build for the operator's actual problem, versus the alternatives, given its external risks, costs and maturity? HV cannot answer this by being more internally consistent; the decisive facts are external to the packet.
11	
12	## 2. What "correct" means here (decision criteria)
13	
14	1. Problem-fit: does the design serve the operator's stated intent (independent nodes; bidirectional sync; Git-style branches IN; merge with mandatory conflict review; two-char node tags; PRs OUT) with low impedance mismatch?
15	2. Best-among-alternatives: among the surfaced options (library-options A-I), is Dolt the best fit for THOSE requirements?
16	3. Critical-dependency feasibility: can the single load-bearing dependency (a maintained EF Core 10 provider driving Dolt over the MySQL wire on net10.0) be satisfied without violating the operator's dependency rules?
17	4. Maturity and operational risk: is the engine production-sound for a small lab that may grow, and what operational burden does it add?
18	5. Complexity vs value (V-squared): is the build proportionate to the value, or over-engineered for two hosts plus a logical test peer?
19	6. Reversibility and lock-in: if the bet is wrong later, how cleanly can the operator get his data back out?
20	7. Sequencing and optionality: can the decision be de-risked by proving the uncertain parts before committing the irreversible ones?
21	
22	## 3. The case FOR (points that this is correct)
23	
24	- 3.1 Best structural fit for the stated requirements (inference, high confidence). The operator asked for branches, three-way merge with review, and retained history on project DATA. Dolt provides commit/branch/merge/clone/fetch/push/pull natively on relational tables. Among the surfaced options, nothing else gives native relational history+branching: Dotmim.Sync is row synchronization with a ServerWins default and no history/branch model; Fossil is a SQLite-backed DVCS but does not map the existing EF business tables; libgit2 SQL backends are a custom-development project, not library reuse. So for the operator's EXACT requirements, Dolt is the strongest fit the research found. (Receipt: library-options.md options D, F, G, H, I.)
25	- 3.2 The plan is structured to answer "correct" before committing (observation). Ph0 is a disposable feasibility harness with twelve blocking outputs (B1-B12), all initial status "unproven," and it explicitly forbids silent EF downgrade, a prerelease provider, or a bespoke provider; it requires reporting concrete alternatives if compatibility fails. Nothing in Ph1-Ph8 is authorized until Ph0 is accepted. So the plan already treats the engine/provider bet as a gated spike, not an assumption. (Receipt: 2026-11-10-federation-dolt-bdpv4.md section 5; architecture.md section 8.)
26	- 3.3 Lock-in is partially mitigated by design (observation). Ph3 delivers a verified all-domain Dolt-to-new-SQLite recovery export (every B2 domain, every branch, dirty working sets), with originals kept read-only and a one-node-first 48-hour soak before the second host. This is a real exit path, not a promise. (Receipt: architecture.md section 9; ac-FullProjectRecoveryPreservesAllDomains.)
27	- 3.4 Dolt is a real, committed engine (observation, from vendor and third parties). Dolt 1.0 shipped in 2023 with a committed storage format and self-describes as production-ready; it supports multi-writer concurrency via standard SQL transactions with a commit/merge layer on top. (Receipt: DoltHub productionizing/concurrency posts.)
28	
29	## 4. The case AGAINST (risks that this may not be correct NOW)

    Generation ordering is scoped to a non-reused HubEpoch. Restore installs a fresh epoch before any endpoint reopens and forces ancestry reconciliation; a node never discards a head because a restored counter is lower. The authenticated worker claims a monotonic WorkerEpoch within the current HubEpoch on reconnect/restart; reports compare epoch and the generation actually observed. A late old-epoch report is rejected. A report for generation g can record its outcome without clearing desired generation g+1. A completed report requires NodeAcceptedHead to include the target and records a durable operation receipt; retries of the same report return that receipt. A transient failure remains unsatisfied with node-local retry scheduling. waiting_local_work, needs_review, incompatible_schema and denied are visible non-success outcomes, not completed requests. Do not add per-message leases, acknowledgement deletion or coalescing machinery to this state table.

    docs/plans/exports/Federation-2026-11-10.html:691:

    Use existing normalized error envelopes with stable codes: head_changed, working_set_changed, branch_busy, waiting_local_work, needs_review, incompatible_schema, unsupported_contract, unauthorized_project, lease_lost, remote_unavailable, migration_verification_failed. Public DTOs and APIs require XMLDocs and OpenAPI documentation. Plugin bootstrap advertises capabilities and server contract version; old plugins fail clearly on unsupported commands without falling back to arbitrary SQL or shell access. Local request authorization uses existing local identities. Hub requests use the existing IdentityServer with per-node client credentials and project scopes; revocation is an IdentityServer action, validated by gateway introspection. It does not erase offline work. See section 13 and TR-MCP-FEDERATION-012.

    docs/plans/exports/Federation-2026-11-10.html:731:

    Append audit locally with an outbox in the same operational transaction as its auditable operation where possible; an explicit recovery scanner covers cross-store crash windows. Deliver through authenticated POST /qbrainai/federation/audit/batches without waiting for a project commit. The hub ledger is append-only and unversioned. It does not replay business commands. Identity is (OriginNodeId,RecordId); exact retry returns the same payload-hash receipt; a changed payload under the same ID returns409 audit_id_conflict. Node and hub runtime roles cannot update/delete existing audit records. Hub indexing is a derived projection.

    docs/plans/exports/Federation-2026-11-10.html:736:

    Review visibility is immediate in server status, all plugins and a durable operator inbox. needs_review and waiting_local_work warn at15minutes, escalate at24hours and repeat no more than hourly. These are local UI/inbox notifications; external messaging requires its existing explicit authorization. Identical edits and mechanically independent cells may merge after domain validation. TODO priority/status/completion, conflicting title/description, dependency deletion and delete/update disagreements require review; no time-based winner. One blocked branch cannot stop another branch/project's publication. Later commits dependent on a blocked branch remain local or move to an explicitly created branch; there is no hidden cherry-pick or discard.

    docs/plans/exports/Federation-2026-11-10.html:845:

    B has uncommitted edits at C0. A publishes A1; B polls and fetches history, but records waiting_local_work instead of committing, discarding or overwriting its draft. B's user finishes the draft and explicitly commits B1 (or separately chooses another authorized disposition). Then reconciliation proceeds. Fetch succeeded does not mean the branch was synchronized. Requirements: FR-MCP-175,180,183,189.

    docs/plans/exports/Federation-2026-11-10.html:859:

    Precondition: A is enrolled in Atlas; main=C0 and A has authorized local audit storage. A edits T1 while offline, appending immutable audit E1 and its outbox entry. On reconnect, audit/batches sends E1 through the IdentityServer gateway, independent of Dolt commits. The hub stores it append-only and returns a hash-bound receipt. A lost receipt causes retry, not duplication; the node retains E1 permanently. Postcondition: one E1 at each origin/hub ledger, main and remote still C0, local draft preserved. Errors: invalid_token, unauthorized_project, audit_id_conflict. Requirements: FR-MCP-AUDIT-001, FR-MCP-184/185/188. Ph2/Ph3/Ph5/Ph7.
